panels.title: Scrape targets up
panels.description: json_exporter has NO probe_success metric. A fetch failure returns HTTP 503 and a config fault panics the handler; in both cases NO samples are ingested at all. `up` is the ONLY signal that a number on this dashboard is stale rather than real. Expect 4 targets.

panels.title: Cost coverage (lifetime)
panels.description: 0 means at least one model in use has NO entry in the LiteLLM price table, so every cost figure below UNDERSTATES real spend. Cost is computed plugin-side against a table refreshed from GitHub every 6h; an unpriced model yields cost_available=false, not an error.

panels.title: Per-model reconciliation
panels.description: Self-audit. sum(per-model requests) / sum(scope totals) should sit at 1.00. It drifts below 1.00 exactly when the summary API's `limit` parameter has truncated models[] - otherwise a completely silent form of undercounting.

panels.title: Credentials in error/disabled
panels.description: Credentials whose status is error or disabled. A DELETED credential vanishes from the API entirely, so its row disappears rather than showing an error state.

panels.title: Lifetime spend (all scopes)
panels.description:
Sums scope=codex + other + xai. These are DISJOINT partitions of the same dataset - reading `totals` alone would hide all Claude spend.

This stat is correct regardless of Prometheus retention because the scraped value is the plugin's own SQLite lifetime sum. By contrast increase(...[30d]) is NOT computable here: prometheus-home-cluster keeps 15d and prometheus-kube-stack 14d.

panels.title: Spend last 24h by model
panels.description: Uses the plugin-computed rolling-window value, not increase()/rate() over a counter. codex-token-usage recomputes cost from the current LiteLLM price map (refreshed every 6h), so *_cost_usd_total can decrease when upstream prices change; Prometheus would read that as a counter reset and report roughly the whole lifetime spend as window spend.

panels.title: Spend last 24h
panels.description: Uses the plugin-computed rolling-window value, not increase()/rate() over a counter. codex-token-usage recomputes cost from the current LiteLLM price map (refreshed every 6h), so *_cost_usd_total can decrease when upstream prices change; Prometheus would read that as a counter reset and report roughly the whole lifetime spend as window spend.

panels.title: Cumulative spend by scope
panels.description: scope=codex is Codex-OAuth only; scope=other is Claude/Gemini/etc; scope=xai is xAI. Disjoint - a cluster total is the SUM of all three.

panels.title: Token mix (rate/sec, all scopes)
panels.description: Cache efficiency at a glance: a healthy Claude Code workload shows cache-read dominating input.

panels.title: Per-provider totals (non-Codex scope)
panels.description: providers[] covers the non-Codex scope only. This is the ONLY per-Claude token/cost breakdown that exists - see the note in the 'Per-account' panel about why per-account Claude data is unavailable.

panels.title: Credentials and quota (Tier 1 - works with no plugin)
Request rate by credential
panels.description: Failures plotted negative. These counters are in-memory in cliproxy and reset to 0 on pod restart - correct counter semantics, handled by rate(). success+failed is NOT a lifetime total.

panels.title: Failure ratio by credential

targets.expr: sum by (provider, email) (rate(cliproxy_auth_requests_failed_total[15m])) / clamp_min(sum by (provider, email) (rate(cliproxy_auth_requests_success_total[15m]) + rate(cliproxy_auth_requests_failed_total[15m])), 0.001)

panels.description: The clamp_min is load-bearing: without it an idle credential gives 0/0 = NaN and the panel flickers to garbage.

panels.title: Credential health
panels.description: A credential that is deleted (or runtime-only and disabled) is OMITTED from the API response entirely, so its row DISAPPEARS rather than showing an error state. Absence is the failure mode to watch.

panels.title: Codex quota used (primary)
panels.description:
CODEX ACCOUNTS ONLY. These fields are omitempty and are genuinely ABSENT for non-Codex credentials, so this panel shows No Data when no Codex account is registered.

AN EMPTY PANEL DOES NOT MEAN QUOTA IS FINE - it means the field was not reported. `or vector(0)` is deliberately NOT used here: it would append a phantom 0% gauge that reads as healthy. Cross-check the credential health table.

panels.title: Average latency / TTFT by scope
panels.description: These are WINDOW MEANS over a rolling 24h, not quantiles. No true latency histogram is available from any non-destructive CLIProxyAPI endpoint, so p95/p99 cannot be computed. Read as gauges - they are deliberately NOT scraped from window=all, where they would be lifetime averages that asymptotically freeze.

panels.title: Slow requests in window
panels.description: Thresholds are fixed upstream: latency_ms >= 12000, ttft_ms >= 3000.

panels.title: Per-account usage
panels.description:
IMPORTANT GAP, do not misread this table. accounts[] in the plugin summary is Codex-scope only; there is NO provider_accounts[] array. Per-account TOKEN and COST data therefore does NOT exist for Claude or Gemini and those rows will simply be missing here.

Per-account REQUEST counts for ALL providers are available in the Tier 1 panels above (cliproxy_auth_requests_*_total), and per-provider Claude tokens/cost are in the 'Per-provider totals' table.
